biomarkers.name: TP53 mutations / loss
biomarkers.prevalence: Very common somatic alteration; germline in Li-Fraumeni syndrome (LFS)
biomarkers.clinical_use: LFS: cascade family testing (osteosarcoma is a core LFS tumour). Osteosarcoma in a young child should trigger LFS consideration

biomarkers.name: RB1 loss
biomarkers.prevalence: Common somatic alteration; germline in hereditary retinoblastoma
biomarkers.clinical_use: RB1 germline carriers have markedly increased osteosarcoma risk — genetic counselling/testing implications

biomarkers.name: Necrosis after neoadjuvant chemo (Huvos grade)
biomarkers.clinical_use: ≥90% necrosis (good response) predicts better outcome; prognostic after preoperative chemotherapy

biomarkers.name: MDM2 / CDK4 amplification
biomarkers.prevalence: Characteristic of low-grade osteosarcoma (including parosteal / low-grade central)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Supports diagnosis of low-grade osteosarcoma and helps distinguish from benign fibro-osseous lesions

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Malignant spindle or pleomorphic cells producing osteoid (unmineralised bone matrix) — defining feature
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Usually high-grade in conventional osteosarcoma; parosteal is low-grade, periosteal is typically intermediate-grade

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Immune-cold typically; TIL infiltration variable and prognostic; IO responses generally modest
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Osteoid production is defining; mineralisation variable

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Mesenchymal stem cells or osteoblast progenitors of bone
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Osteoblastic differentiation with defining osteoid (unmineralised bone matrix) production; osteoblastic (~70%), chondroblastic (with cartilaginous component), fibroblastic subtypes reflect differentiation heterogeneity
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Complex karyotype with chromothripsis and genomic instability; TP53 and RB1 pathway alterations are very common; MDM2/CDK4 amplification occurs in low-grade parosteal/low-grade central variants
